macros.name: afterRef
macros.doc: \afterRef is the space that follows the passage reference.

macros.name: cobblevrs
macros.doc: \cobblevrs takes ⟨text⟩ and adds it to the end of the text macro ⟨\cmd⟩.

macros.name: cobblevrs*
macros.doc: \cobblevrs takes ⟨text⟩ and adds it to the end of the text macro ⟨\cmd⟩.

macros.name: fbdefaultBible
macros.doc: The command \fbdefaultBible holds the (current) default Bible abbreviation.

macros.name: fbResetMarParFmt
macros.doc: If \fbMarParFmt is redefined, then expanding \fbResetMarParFmt returns it to its original definition.

macros.name: fetchversestxt
macros.doc: The \fetchversestxt command does not expand to typeset content, rather, it defines two commands \versetxt, which contains the verse reference, and \passagetxt, which contains the passage for that verse.

macros.name: fetchversestxt
macros.doc: The \fetchversestxt command does not expand to typeset content, rather, it defines two commands \versetxt, which contains the verse reference, and \passagetxt, which contains the passage for that verse.

macros.name: gobbleto
macros.doc: The command defines another command ⟨\cmd⟩, the action of this command is to gobble up all token between it and the ⟨word⟩.

macros.name: resetAfterBookSpc
macros.doc: The command \resetAfterBookSpc resets \fb@bksp to its default.

macros.name: sr
macros.doc: \sr is a command that takes two arguments, if the first one is non-empty, the ⟨text⟩ argument appears in italics.

macros.name: translFmt
macros.doc: To change the default formatting for \fetchverses and \fetchverse, use the \translFmt command.

macros.name: translFmtDef
macros.doc: Reset to the default definition by expanding \translFmtDef.

macros.name: verseCmts
macros.doc: The \verseCmts command is used to define the notes (comments), each note corresponds to a verse.

macros.name: verseFmt
macros.doc: The definition of \verseFmt determines the formatting of the verse number in the passage; the argument of \verseFmt (#1) is the verse number.

macros.name: verseFmtDef
macros.doc: \verseFmtDef is the default command to typeset the verse numbers as a superscript.

envs.name: declareBVs
envs.doc: The declareBVs and declareBVs* environments may be used anywhere in the document – preamble or body – to declare Biblical verses.

envs.name: declareBVs*
envs.doc: The declareBVs and declareBVs* environments may be used anywhere in the document – preamble or body – to declare Biblical verses.
